patches.find: Park at the Blue Lake Trailhead (about 5,200 ft, Northwest Forest Pass required), on the south side of the highway roughly 1.5 miles west of the Washington Pass overlook. Follow the Blue Lake Trail #314 about 1.5 miles to a small meadow, then branch off left onto the well-worn climbers' path, which climbs steeply through slabs, talus, and meadow (with short 3rd-class scrambling) into the basin below the Liberty Bell Group — roughly 3 miles and 2,000 ft of gain, 1.5-2.5 hours total. The classic Beckey Route starts from the notch (about 7,300 ft) between Liberty Bell and Concord Tower, reached via the gully splitting off the climbers' path.
patches.replace: Park beside the small pond on SR-20 a few hundred yards east of Washington Pass (about 5,400 ft). Walk around the pond's left side and take the climbers' path into the forest, heading roughly south-southwest; it comes out onto talus beneath the east walls of Liberty Bell and Minuteman near 6,000 ft. Work up the talus to Minuteman's lower left corner, around 6,600 ft. Plan on about an hour and roughly 1,200 ft of climbing from the car.

patches.expect: Two established descents, both about 5 rappels, which is why the stored figures differed. One published West Face description: "Three single rope raps bring you down to the notch, another gets you off the large chockstone (a fun, free-hanging rappel), and some scrambling and down-climbing (or a short 30 foot rap on a tree) get you back on the ground", and separately "There is four fairly new bolted rap stations and a tree rappel for the last section." A 60 m rope just barely works on the bolted line; 70 m is more comfortable.
patches.value: Two established descents. The bolted West Face line is six bolted single-rope stations; a 60 m rope only just reaches and a 70 m is the comfortable choice. The classic line is three single-rope rappels to the notch, a free-hanging double-rope rappel past the chockstone, then a short tree rappel or a downclimb to the ground; the table below lists the classic line.
